04 / FROM ZERO TO LOCALHOST

Your next app starts here.

A few commands.
A lot less configuration.

FROM YOUR PROJECT FOLDER
# Serve your Laravel application
laraserve serve ./my-app

# Prefer plain HTTP? You’re in control.
laraserve serve ./my-app --http

First use needs internet to download the runtime. Follow the terminal prompts to trust the local certificate.

Need the executable? Build from the LaraServe project with Go 1.21+: make buildYour client: bin/laraserve
A FEW THINGS TO KNOW
Does it install PHP or MySQL globally?+

No. Runtimes live in LaraServe’s cache, and managed MySQL uses a private Unix socket. Tools download on first use, with SHA-256 verification.

Can I keep my existing database connection?+

Yes. Use laraserve serve --mysql=false to keep your external connection. Automatic MySQL mode creates a separate local database; it does not import existing data.

Does it install Node or build frontend assets?+

Frontend assets need your own Node tooling. Build them before serving or packing an app that requires them. LaraServe manages PHP, Composer, MySQL, and phpMyAdmin.

What if the browser shows a certificate warning?+

Run laraserve trust and restart your browser. On Linux, Firefox trust may need the certutil tool from libnss3-tools or nss-tools. Use --http to serve without certificate setup.
